fixes: Dek corrected: the 30–40 percent figure is one implementing partner's estimate reported by SIGAR, not a SIGAR finding
The finding that UN cash shipments stabilized the economy but benefited the Taliban is from SIGAR-24-32-IP (July 2024), not 24-12
'$1.6 billion UN' sentence replaced with SIGAR's wording (the audit could not examine U.S. money routed through UN agencies; the $10.9 million is 'probably a gross undercount')
$3.83 billion clarified: about 36 percent of all international aid since August 2021
edits: SIGAR: maybe 30 to 40 percent of donor funds reaches the population.
An aid partner told SIGAR maybe 30 to 40 percent of donor funds reaches the population.
More than **$3.83 billion** in humanitarian and development assistance went into that country.

**$3.83 billion** in U.S. humanitarian and development assistance went into that country, about 36 percent of all international aid, per [SIGAR](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-S-PURL-gpo248012/pdf/GOVPUB-S-PURL-gpo248012.pdf).
SIGAR found those shipments stabilized an economy the Taliban ran — and benefited the Taliban.
A later SIGAR inspection (SIGAR-24-32-IP, July 2024) found those shipments stabilized the Afghan economy but benefit the Taliban.
SIGAR said that figure is a fraction. The UN took about **$1.6 billion** in U.S. funding for Afghanistan in that window and did not report the taxes its subawardees paid.
SIGAR said the figure was “probably a gross undercount”: the audit could not examine U.S. money routed through UN agencies, because the UN does not collect that data from its implementing partners.
